verification.output:
Both findings trace to the same removed block in `Lib/ipaddress.py` (`_parse_octet`). The diff deletes the only guard against leading-zero octets (the block whose comment cites bpo-36384), and the remaining code `int(octet_str, 10)` unconditionally parses leading-zero strings as decimal, so inputs like `'017'`, `'010'`, `'000'` that previously raised `ValueError` now parse successfully. I attempted to disprove by looking for any compensating check elsewhere in the diff: none exists — the hunk only removes lines, and the length/digits/`> 255` checks do not reject leading zeros. The misinterpretation scenario (decimal here vs. octal downstream) follows directly from `int(octet_str, 10)` accepting what glibc `inet_pton`-style parsers read as octal, which is exactly the ambiguity the removed check's own comment said it prevented.
